summary.name: AirStats
summary.one_liner: AirStats is a free, open source, lightweight menu bar system monitor for macOS that shows up to sixteen metrics such as CPU, GPU, memory, network, disk, battery and temperature.
use_cases: Watch CPU, memory and network load at a glance from the menu bar
Check which processes are using resources via the top processes panel
Pin a desktop widget showing metrics you always want visible
Get notified when a metric crosses a threshold you set
Compare resource overhead against other Mac monitoring apps
summary.what_it_does: AirStats puts up to sixteen system metrics in the Mac menu bar, and you can choose to show just two or all sixteen. Clicking the menu bar item opens a panel with per core CPU load, memory pressure and top processes. Metrics can also be pinned as a desktop widget, with a colour per metric. Threshold alerts send a notification when a chosen metric crosses a level you set, and keyboard shortcuts open the panel or widget. Each detailed metric (per core load, memory pressure, GPU, network, disk, battery, temperature, top processes) keeps the last 24 hours of history. The source is MIT licensed and the page says it runs as one process with no helper or launch agent.
notable: Sixteen menu bar metrics in a single process with no helper or launch agent, about 8.9 MB
Open source under MIT license, including the benchmark scripts
Compared against Stats and iStat Menus in the page's benchmark
caveats: Apple silicon only; no Intel Mac support yet
Public IP lookup is optional and off by default, and it sends data when enabled
